sources.supports: Bibliographic coupling is a document relationship/grouping technique; its groups are not themselves an assessment of historical seminalness.
sources.does_not_establish: A validated seminal-paper classifier or substantive adaptive-leadership appraisal

sources.inspected_scope: author-deposited review abstract and version metadata
sources.supports: Citation indicators require explicit publication/citation inclusion and normalization decisions, including field differences.
sources.does_not_establish: That dividing citations by age is valid field normalization

sources.inspected_scope: publisher full HTML, abstract and discussion through document-type normalization
sources.supports: Citation opportunity varies by field, publication age, document type and database coverage; counts can reflect several kinds of attention. Fine-grained normalization and recent cohorts can be noisy.
sources.does_not_establish: Citations as article quality, causal effect, conceptual novelty or universal historical influence

design_implication: Use complementary descriptive signals and content appraisal. Keep global snapshot counts distinct from observed within-corpus incoming citations, coupling similarity and cited-reference frequency. Keep unknown coverage visible, inspect age and type, and avoid a single invented seminalness score.

not_acquired.status: publisher fetch timeout; no full text read claim
